name: Śrīnidhi
text:
## In short

Śrīnidhi, the youngest brother of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, one of the «four brothers» of Navadvīpa who chanted Kṛṣṇa's names day and night.

## In the book

«Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and his three brothers continually chanted the names of Kṛṣṇa. They would take three baths daily in the Gaṅgā and then worship Lord Kṛṣṇa» (Ādi 2.97). The *bhāṣya* on Ādi 2.97: «The words *cāri bhāi* refer to Śrīvāsa, Śrīrāma, Śrīpati, and Śrīnidhi» — the four brothers who «continually chanted the names of Kṛṣṇa» and «would take three baths daily in the Gaṅgā and then worship Lord Kṛṣṇa». When Advaita spoke of the people's ridicule of the devotees, «particularly the four brothers headed by Śrīvāsa» were mocked for their chanting (Ādi 11, chapter summary).

When the Lord revealed Himself in Śrīvāsa's house, «Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita led his brothers, wife, servants, and maidservants in humbly falling at the lotus feet of the Lord» (Madhya 2.301).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 2.97 (with bhāṣya); 11 (chapter summary); Madhya 2.301.

name: Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita
text:
## In short

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, the eldest of four brothers of Navadvīpa — Nārada in Kṛṣṇa-līlā, says the *Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā* —, in whose courtyard the Lord inaugurated saṅkīrtana and revealed Himself; his house sheltered Nityānanda; when his son died during the kīrtana, he forbade the household to weep so as not to disturb the Lord.

## The four brothers (Ādi 2.34, 2.96–97)

«Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita resided in Navadvīpa. Lord Caitanya enjoyed many pastimes in his house. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and his three brothers continually chanted the names of Kṛṣṇa.» The *bhāṣya* on Ādi 2.97: «The words *cāri bhāi* refer to Śrīvāsa, Śrīrāma, Śrīpati, and Śrīnidhi» — the four brothers who «continually chanted the names of Kṛṣṇa» and «would take three baths daily in the Gaṅgā and then worship Lord Kṛṣṇa». When Advaita spoke of the people's ridicule of the devotees, «particularly the four brothers headed by Śrīvāsa» were mocked for their chanting (Ādi 11, chapter summary). The *bhāṣya* (Ādi 2.34) quotes the *Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā* (90): Śrīvāsa is Nārada Muni and Śrīrāma is Parvata Muni; after the Lord's sannyāsa they left Navadvīpa and lived at **Kumārahaṭṭa**. His courtyard is «nondifferent from Śrī Vṛndāvana» (*bhāṣya* 2.96).

## The Lord reveals Himself (Madhya 2.257–323)

The Lord kicked again and again at the door of the room where Śrīvāsa was worshipping Nṛsiṁhadeva; Śrīvāsa saw a blazing fire, opened his eyes and trembled, speechless. Reassured, «Śrīvāsa Pandita was a natural scholar and a *mahā-bhāgavata*. Having been ordered by the Lord, he offered heartfelt prayers… similar to those offered by Brahmā». The Lord had him bring his family: «Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita led his brothers, wife, servants, and maidservants in humbly falling at the lotus feet of the Lord», and then turned to his little niece Nārāyaṇī. (Earlier, Madhya 2, he had told Śacī that her son's state was not a nervous malady but the highest devotion.)

## Faith in Nityānanda (Madhya 8.6–23)

Nityānanda lived in his house as a child, calling him «father» and Mālinī «mother». To test him the Lord asked why he kept an *avadhūta* of unknown caste. Śrīvāsa said that even if Nityānanda drank wine, associated with prostitutes or destroyed his caste and wealth, his faith would not waver: «I know Nityānanda is Your own body.» The Lord roared, embraced him — «O Paṇḍita Śrīvāsa, what did you say? You have so much faith in Nityānanda?» — and blessed him that even if Lakṣmī had to beg, he would never be poor, and even the cats and dogs of his house would have devotion to Him.

## Other moments

- **Devānanda's class** (Madhya 9.90–96; 21.59–66): his heart melted hearing the *Bhāgavatam*, and the students dragged him out.
- **The drama** (Madhya 18.11, 18.61–64): he played Nārada — «Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita looked just like Nārada, with the same form, same words».
- **His son's death** (Madhya 25 — chapter summary): during the kīrtana in his courtyard his son died; hearing the ladies cry, he went in and told them to stop their mundane lamentation so that the Lord's ecstasy would not be disturbed — or he would drown himself in the Gaṅgā — and rejoined the kīrtana. The Lord, sensing a calamity, learned of it, wept at his love, made the dead boy speak on spiritual knowledge, and promised that He and His brother would remain in Śrīvāsa's house as his sons.
- **«Everything will come to your doorstep»** (Antya 5.50–65): when Śrīvāsa said that if he got no food for three days he would tie a pot to his neck and drown in the Gaṅgā, the Lord roared: «Even if Lakṣmī has to beg, your household will not be afflicted by poverty… O Śrīnivāsa, you just sit happily at home. Everything will come to your doorstep. My benediction to Advaita and you is that your bodies will never be affected by old age.» And to Śrīrāma: «You should never give up the service of Śrīvāsa» (5.66–68).
- **A leper's offense** (Antya 4, chapter summary): a leper who had offended Śrīvāsa was told by the Lord that his only remedy was to beg Śrīvāsa's forgiveness; by Śrīvāsa's mercy he was freed.
- To Purī: he splashed water with the devotees (Antya 8.125–126).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 2.34, 2.96–97 (with bhāṣya); Madhya 2.257–323 and chapter summary; 8.6–23; 9.90–96; 18.11, 18.61–64; 21.59–66; 25 (chapter summary); Antya 4 (chapter summary); 5.50–70; 8.125–126.
